speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history of chronic cough and recurrent bronchitis. To understand the root cause, can you tell me exactly how long you've had these symptoms and what specifically triggers the coughing fits?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is a remarkably long duration for these symptoms, especially given your history of recurrent bronchitis. You mentioned the sputum is thick, foamy, and yellow-green, and that you are a non-smoker; have you noticed any wheezing, shortness of breath, or hemoptysis (coughing up blood)?

text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: NORMAL READINGS, Sputum_Culture: Heavy growth of non-specific bacteria, no TB or fungal growth, Alpha_1_Antitrypsin_Level: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Aggressive cough with thick, yellow-green sputum. I also have Cough worse in the morning, History of recurrent bronchitis. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis.

The mention of Pyelonephritis by another doctor is clinically inconsistent with your respiratory symptoms and chronic sputum production; we must focus on the lung findings. Please describe if you have ever had a lung CT scan or if you have noticed any post-nasal drip or sinus issues in the past?
